la:adj:Papirius.html:
Păpīrĭus, i (old form Păpīsĭus, ; Paul. ex ; Müll.), m.,
the name of a patrician and plebeian gens, .—Thus,
The dictator, L. Papirius Cursor, ; . 1.—
C. Papirius Carbo, the friend of Ti. Gracchus, ; ; ; ; . —Hence,
Păpīrĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Papirius, Papirian: Papiria lex,: tribus,one of the rural tribes,; ; Müll.; et saep.—
Păpīrĭānus, a, um, adj., Papirian: domus,: saevitia,; cf. : jus civile Papirianum, a juridical compilation of S. Papirius, .

la:noun:papaver.html:
păpāver, ĕris, n. (ante-class., m.) [etym. dub.; cf. root pa- of pasco, πέπαμαι],
the poppy.
Lit.: papaver Gallicanus, Cato ap. P.: sesamum papaveremque,; v.infra, prov.; Varr. ap. : luteum,: spargens soporiferum papaver,; : Lethaeo perfusa papavera somno,: Cereale,: nigrum,; . —In plur.: summa papaverum capita,the heads of the tallest poppies,; Petr. poët. 132, 11.—Prov.: confit cito, Quam si formicis tu obicias papaverem, of any thing that quickly disappears,.—
Transf., a kernel, seed: papaver fici,fig-seed,.—
Trop.: dicta quasi papavere et sesamo sparsa,

la:noun:pappus.html:
pappus, i, m., = πάππος.
An old man, Müll.—
A grandfather, .—
The woolly, hairy seed of certain plants, Lachm.; also ap. Müll.: semen ei lanuginis, quam pappon vocant,.—
A plant, also called erigeron: quare eam Callimachus acanthida appellat, alii pappum,.

la:adj:Papius.gloss: of or pertaining to the gens Papia.
senses: of or pertaining to the gens Papia.
la:adj:Papius.html:
Pāpĭus, i, m.,
the name of a Roman gens.—
C. Papius, a tribune of the people, the originator of the lex Papia de peregrinis exterminandis, .—
M. Papius Mutilus, a consul, who, together with his colleague, Poppaeus, passed, in the reign of Augustus, the lex Papia Poppaea, for the promotion of marriages, ; ; ; suet. ; ; .—
Papia, wife of Oppianicus, .—Hence, Pāpĭus, a, adj., of or belonging to the gens Papia: Papia tribus,; et saep.
